learningJourney.title: What is Data Mesh
learningJourney.explanation:
**Data Mesh** applies Domain-Driven Design (DDD) and platform engineering to analytical data. Instead of dumping operational databases into a central monolith owned by a separate data team, each business domain (Orders, Ledger, Inventory) owns its analytical datasets end-to-end.

It rests on four pillars: (1) **Domain Ownership**, (2) **Data as a Product** (discoverable, versioned, SLA-backed), (3) **Self-Serve Data Platform** (Terraform/CLI templates for Iceberg, Kafka, IAM, lineage), and (4) **Federated Computational Governance** (automated CI/CD and runtime policies, not manual review boards).
learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how Data Mesh works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: Why Centralized Warehouses Collapse at Organizational Scale
learningJourney.explanation: A single central data engineering team cannot understand the domain semantics of 40+ upstream microservices—leading to brittle ETL scrapers, silent schema breakages, and 6-week backlogs for simple metric updates.

learningJourney.title: How to manage Data Product Anatomy & Policy-as-Code
learningJourney.explanation: Every data product exposes **Input Ports** (CDC/Kafka), **Transformation Logic** (dbt/Spark/Flink), **Polyglot Output Ports** (batch Apache Iceberg + streaming Kafka topic sharing one canonical schema), and a **Control Port** (OpenLineage + Prometheus freshness lag). Federated governance runs as OPA/Conftest checks in CI and dynamic row/column masking in Trino/Unity Catalog.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```yaml
# Open Data Contract Standard (ODCS) snippet enforced by OPA in CI
kind: DataProduct
name: checkout.orders.v2
owner: checkout-platform@acme.io
slo:
  freshnessMinutes: 10
  completenessPct: 99.9
schema:
  compatibility: BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE
  columns:
    - name: order_id
      type: string
      unique: true
    - name: customer_email
      type: string
      classification: PII
      maskingPolicy: sha256_hash
```

knowledgeCheck.question: A company adopts Data Mesh by letting 12 domain teams dump raw Postgres tables directly into S3 buckets without schemas or catalog registration, while creating a 15-person committee to manually review every new dataset. What two failure modes did they hit?

options.text: Siloed Data Swamps and Governance Theater
options.feedback: Correct: missing automated catalog/contract gates creates data swamps, and manual review boards destroy domain velocity instead of using computational governance.
Those are storage/concurrency failure modes, not organizational Data Mesh failure modes.
Those belong to CPU profiling, not Data Mesh.
